narrative: tjce-verify is a well-architected 4-layer verification orchestrator with clean separation of concerns, robust headless mode, and mature deterministic scripts. The primary improvement areas are a structured data pipeline gap where the LLM performs ~2,000 tokens of deterministic formatting work, missing error recovery for infrastructure failures, and stage/layer numbering inconsistencies. One latent integrity risk exists: unparseable coverage silently passes the coverage gate.

broken.title: Coverage null-pass: unparseable coverage silently bypasses the coverage gate
broken.detail: When extract_coverage() returns None (malformed report), determine_verdict() treats it as not-below-threshold and can return GO. This contradicts the non-negotiable: 'Cobertura abaixo de {coverage_threshold}% = bloqueio automatico.'
broken.action: Add guard: if coverage is None, return NO-GO with diagnostic 'Coverage could not be determined. Treated as blocking condition.'

opportunities.name: Structured Data Pipeline Gap
opportunities.description: The skill's scripts produce structured JSON, but the LLM performs ~2,000 tokens per run of deterministic JSON-to-markdown formatting. The consolidation script re-parses its own markdown with brittle regex. This root cause also enables the coverage null-pass bug.
opportunities.impact: Eliminates ~2,000 tokens of deterministic LLM work per run, removes regex brittleness, closes the coverage null-pass integrity risk.
opportunities.action: Create format-security-report.py, extend consolidate-results.py with --format markdown, expose extract_coverage() as CLI subcommand, add None guard to verdict logic.
findings: Security report markdown assembly: LLM merges two JSON outputs into markdown (L6-F4, high, 500-800 tokens)
Verify summary markdown formatting: LLM templates consolidation JSON into markdown (L6-F5, high, 500-700 tokens)
Consolidation regex parsing: script re-parses markdown instead of consuming JSON sidecars (L3-F8, medium)
Coverage re-parsing at Stage 2: same extraction already exists in consolidation script (L6-F1, medium, 200-300 tokens)
Layer 1 report formatting: structured data formatted as markdown by LLM (L6-F6, medium, 300-500 tokens)
Coverage null-pass: None coverage silently passes the gate (L4/L5, latent high)
Config note duplication across references: ~90 tokens of redundant explanation (L2-F01, medium)
Cycle report completeness validation: 70% deterministic cross-referencing done by LLM (L6-F3, medium)

opportunities.name: Missing Error Recovery Layer
opportunities.description: The skill does not distinguish between 'verification found problems' and 'a tool crashed.' Script failures, agent unavailability, and infrastructure issues manifest as ambiguous exit code 1 or undefined behavior.
opportunities.impact: Prevents false blocking verdicts from tool crashes, provides clear diagnostics for infrastructure issues, enables graceful degradation.
opportunities.action: Validate JSON output presence as primary signal (missing JSON = tool failure). Add pre-flight check for Python, script executability, agent availability. Define degradation tiers.
findings: No error recovery for tjce-agent-qa invocation failure (L4-F2, moderate)
Security report format contract undocumented -- consolidation regex may silently misparse (L4-F4, moderate)
Script failure exit code 1 is indistinguishable from 'findings found' exit code 1 (L5, moderate)
No pre-flight check for runtime dependencies: Python, scripts, agent availability (L5, moderate)
Stale cycle report pickup: no validation that cycle report matches current run (L5, low)

opportunities.name: Naming and Numbering Inconsistency
opportunities.description: The skill uses both 'Stage 1-6' and 'Camada 1-4' numbering systems that collide. Stage 4 is security but Camada 4 is human gate. The Output Artifacts table misattributes producers to layers.
opportunities.impact: Reduces model confusion during orchestration, makes the skill self-documenting for maintainers, eliminates the unused user_name variable.
opportunities.action: Rename the Camada column to Descricao in the Execution Flow table. Align Output Artifacts table with the 4-layer model. Wire user_name into APROVADO action or remove it from config.
findings: Output Artifacts table layer numbering does not match 4-layer model (L1-F2, medium)
Stage/Camada numbering collision between SKILL.md table and reference file labels (L2-F06, medium)
Dual numbering system creates confusion for newcomers (L4-F1, low)
Unused {user_name} variable declared in On Activation but never consumed (L1-F1, medium)

opportunities.name: Parallelism Not Leveraged
opportunities.description: Stages 3 (functional) and 4 (security) are independent but run sequentially. Security scripts are documented as parallelizable but invoked without parallel syntax.
opportunities.impact: Reduces wall-clock time by 25-40% on typical runs. Saves 15-30s from stage-level parallelism plus 2-5s from script batching.
opportunities.action: Add explicit parallel execution instructions for Stages 3+4. Provide parallel invocation syntax or instruct LLM to issue parallel Bash tool calls for security scripts.
findings: Stages 3 (functional) and 4 (security) are sequential but have no data dependency (L3-F1, medium)
Security scripts not batched as parallel Bash calls despite being documented as independent (L3-F2, medium)

opportunities.name: UX and Resilience Gaps
opportunities.description: No first-timer orientation, no state persistence across context compaction, no progress indicators, no JSON verdict for automation, and no resume capability for the human gate.
opportunities.impact: Reduces entry friction for new users, enables headless-to-interactive handoff, prevents state loss during compaction, provides machine-readable output for CI/CD.
opportunities.action: Add intent-before-ingestion preamble. Introduce verify-state.json for state checkpointing. Surface verify-verdict.json. Add --continue flag for human gate resume.
findings: No orientation for first-time users: no explanation of what will happen or time estimate (L5, medium)
No state persistence: context compaction can lose which stages passed and their results (L5, medium)
No progress indicators in headless mode for long-running pipelines (L5, low)
No JSON verdict artifact for programmatic consumption by automation (L5, medium)
No --continue flag: headless exits at human gate with no re-entry path (L5, medium)

strengths.title: Clean orchestrator identity
strengths.detail: The skill explicitly states it does not execute tests or code review -- it orchestrates. Delegation boundaries to tjce-agent-qa and scripts are enforced consistently with 'do not duplicate' instructions at cognitive risk points.

strengths.title: Robust headless contract
strengths.detail: Three distinct exit codes (0/1/2) with well-defined semantics, explicit behavior at every interaction point, and a clear 'never automate human gate' invariant make CI/CD integration straightforward.

strengths.title: Exemplary progressive disclosure
strengths.detail: SKILL.md is ~843 tokens. Reference files load on-demand as stages progress. Only the relevant stage occupies the context window -- the gold standard for multi-stage orchestration.

strengths.title: Compaction-resilient architecture
strengths.detail: The Inegociaveis section provides a compaction-survival anchor with maximum signal density: bold formatting, one rule per line, critical rules survive aggressive summarization.

strengths.title: Mature deterministic scripts
strengths.detail: All 4 Python scripts follow a uniform contract: JSON output, exit code discipline (0=pass, 1=fail), --output/--verbose flags, and unit tests. Consistent schema across all scripts.

strengths.title: Graduated blocking strategy
strengths.detail: Three distinct blocking points at different boundaries: pre-check (artifacts), coverage gate (metrics), security gate (critical findings). Non-critical findings flow through to consolidation, maximizing information for the PO.

strengths.title: Zero waste patterns
strengths.detail: No instances of defensive or supplicant language (make sure, remember to, you should, please) across all files. Directives are clean and imperative throughout.

structure.summary: All structural requirements met. Frontmatter correct, required sections present, config integration works, headless contract specified, progression signals in all references. Prepass critical was a false positive (references/ routing pattern, not numbered stage files).

findings.detail: Table lists Camada 1-3 but the 4-layer model maps differently. Camada assignments do not match Overview description.

findings.detail: Same unused variables as functional-and-security.md.

craft.summary: Excellent prompt craft. Total surface is 241 lines across 4 files, well within budget. Progressive disclosure is textbook. Delegation boundaries are marked at cognitive risk points. No waste patterns detected. Two medium findings around redundancy and numbering.

findings.title: Config note duplication across all three references
findings.detail: ~90 tokens of redundant config resolution explanation repeated in each reference. Already established by SKILL.md On Activation.

findings.title: Stage/Camada numbering collision
findings.detail: SKILL.md table uses 'Camada' column with descriptions, but references use 'Camada N' as numeric labels. Stage 4 (security) collides with Camada 4 (human gate).

findings.title: Headless exit-code semantics stated in three locations
findings.detail: Overview, Inegociaveis, and Headless Contract all mention exit codes. Borderline intentional for compaction survival.

findings.title: Missing terminal progression signal in consolidation-and-gate.md
findings.detail: First two references end with explicit progression signals. The terminal reference lacks a 'Workflow complete' closing signal.

cohesion.summary: Stage flow is coherent, purpose alignment is strong, complexity is appropriate. Strong scores on 4 of 6 dimensions, moderate on Gap & Redundancy (missing error recovery) and External Skill Integration (no graceful degradation when tjce-agent-qa unavailable).

findings.title: No error recovery for agent invocation failure
findings.detail: Workflow defines NO-GO behavior but not agent crash/timeout/unavailability behavior. Pre-check validates BUILD artifacts but not agent availability.

findings.title: Security report format contract undocumented
findings.detail: LLM assembles security-report.md from JSON, but consolidation script parses it with regex expecting pipe-delimited severity rows. Format deviation causes silent data loss.

findings.title: Stage numbering vs layer numbering creates mild confusion
findings.detail: Dual numbering (stages 1-6 vs camadas 1-4) is internally consistent but newcomers could conflate Stage 4 with Camada 4.

efficiency.summary: Intentionally sequential design with correct fail-fast ordering. Cheap pre-checks run before expensive operations. Lazy reference loading conserves context. Three concrete optimizations could reduce wall-clock time by 25-40%.

findings.title: Stages 3 and 4 are sequential but independent
findings.detail: Functional verification (subagent) and security scanning (scripts) have no data dependency. Parallel execution saves 15-30s.

findings.title: Security scripts not batched as parallel calls
findings.detail: Two scripts documented as independent but invoked sequentially. Parallel saves 2-5s.

findings.title: Consolidation re-parses markdown with regex instead of consuming JSON
findings.detail: Earlier stages produce structured data serialized to markdown then re-parsed. JSON sidecars would eliminate regex brittleness.

findings.title: Orchestrator re-parses subagent markdown for coverage
findings.detail: Coverage percentage extracted by LLM at Stage 2 when tjce-agent-qa could return structured JSON via --json flag.

experience.summary: User journey analysis across 6 archetypes reveals high entry friction for first-timers, no delta awareness on re-runs, no state persistence, and a human gate island where headless cannot hand off to interactive. The coverage null-pass is the most consequential finding.

findings.title: Coverage null-pass: unparseable coverage silently bypasses gate
findings.detail: extract_coverage() returning None causes determine_verdict() to pass. Directly contradicts the non-negotiable coverage gate.

findings.title: No state persistence across context compaction
findings.detail: Orchestrator state lives in LLM conversation. Context compaction can lose which stages passed and their results. No verify-state.json checkpoint.

findings.title: Script failure indistinguishable from verification findings
findings.detail: All scripts use exit 1 for both 'findings found' and 'script crashed.' Orchestrator cannot distinguish tool failure from verification result.

findings.title: No first-timer orientation or intent confirmation
findings.detail: Pipeline starts immediately on activation. No explanation of what will happen, time estimate, or confirmation of scope. High friction for confused users.

findings.title: Human gate is an island: no headless-to-interactive bridge
findings.detail: Headless generates summary and exits. No --continue flag to resume at human gate. PO decision cannot re-enter the system programmatically.

findings.title: No JSON verdict artifact for automation
findings.detail: Consolidation produces JSON internally but only surfaces markdown. Automators must parse markdown to extract verdicts.

Six opportunities to extract deterministic LLM work into scripts, totaling ~2,000 tokens per run. Two high-severity: security report assembly (500-800 tokens) and verify summary formatting (500-700 tokens).
